newsitem.title: UK: George - BoE will signal rate moves as soon as able.
newsitem.headline: George - BoE will signal rate moves as soon as able.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday that any change in interest rates resulting from his monthly monetary policy meetings would be signalled to financial markets as soon as possible.

"Just as they have discovered in the United States and at the Bundesbank that you really have to inform the markets straight away, so we have actually found that it is almost inconceiveable that you could have any reason for delaying the implementation of a decision to change (rates)," George told parliament's Treasury select committee.
"That is tantamount to saying that the next time we operate in the market (after the end of a monetary meeting), we will actually signal the outcome of the meeting," he said.

Britain's financial markets go through a monthly nail-biting ritual after George meets with Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, waiting for any signalled rate change through the Bank's money market operations.
Often in the past, their meetings have finished so close to the Bank's set operating times, that uncertainty remains about whether a move has been agreed.
